title: One clue or several?
hook: Identification improves when observations are combined.

knows: Birds have body structures and interact with their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: Both schematic birds have red heads, but only the second has wing stripes. Combining field marks distinguishes the two pictured examples; real identification can also require range, behavior, season and other evidence.

misconception: The observed arrangement has a different effect than the one shown.
objective: A field guide shows two birds with red heads, but only one also has a striped wing. Which observation best separates the two in this example?

claims.text: Identification improves when observations are combined. A field guide shows two birds with red heads, but only one also has a striped wing. Which observation best separates the two in this example? Both schematic birds have red heads, but only the second has wing stripes. Combining field marks distinguishes the two pictured examples; real identification can also require range, behavior, season and other evidence.
